executive_assessment.text: A purposive 2025 survey adds named-site detail on flood-related movement and constraints on acting on warnings in Bujumbura, Cibitoke and Makamba.
Colline-level planning and WFP capacity commitments describe institutional responses, not proven delivery or resilience effects; the land-tension mechanism remains a planning hypothesis.

geographic_notes.text: The November 2024 appraisal proposed 71 locations covering 65 hotspot collines in seven provinces; six clearly readable names are Cibitoke, Gitega, Kirundo, Kayanza, Bujumbura and Muyinga.
Among 1,027 purposively selected climate-affected IDPs interviewed in Bujumbura, Cibitoke and Makamba in 2025, 63% reported flood impacts, 34% landslides and 34% unpredictable weather.
Among surveyed IDPs affected by floods, 96% said housing destruction or damage prompted movement; 22% also cited household food or water scarcity.

In the purposive sample, 91% reported no early-warning system. Of 92 respondents who received some warning, 37% could not act because of limited resources; crop and livestock adaptation were uncommon and often ineffective.

known_gaps.text: Automated machine-screening is not independent source verification or human approval. 13 of 13 evidence records and 1 of 1 pathways lack claim-level verification in this remediation; review the linked records before relying on them.
No current subnational climate-impact dataset was opened; the cited vulnerability material is from the 2015 INDC and 2022 report.

National and selected local examples do not establish district-level coverage or causal attribution.
Composite modeled risk categories are not observed climate impacts.

Available evidence supports climate-related internal displacement and a source-stated scarce-land/social-cohesion pathway, but current conflict-specific constraints on household adaptation were not established.
The MMC sample was purposive and concentrated in Bujumbura and Cibitoke; the source warns it is not representative of national mobility dynamics.
The World Bank project document is an appraisal-stage design, so its local capacity measures remain planned rather than evaluated.
Appraisal commitments are dated to November 2024; the 2025 MMC survey is historical and purposive, not a current national prevalence estimate.
